programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc: Tha rudeigin neo-àbhaisteach air tuiteam gu talamh an-diugh. Ach dè idir a th’ ann? Something unusual has fallen to the ground today. What on earth could it be?

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Oona airson 's gun ionnsaich May dhith mar a ni i leum fìor, fìor àrd ach chan eil cùisean a dol leatha 's tha am buthaid bheag a fàs diombach! Ge-tà, tha plan aig Mossy gus sealltainn dha charaid g' eil sgilean sònraichte aice-se cuideachd. Oona wants May to show her how to jump high, but when the lessons don't go to plan, Oona is left frustrated. However, Mossy has a plan to show her that she also has special skills of her own.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Oona 's Silky a coimhead air n-adhart ri latha spòrsail ach le Oona airson a bhith àrd sna speur 's Silky ag iarraidh gu gruund na mara, 's ann a tha iad a strì geama a lorg a tha cheart cho spòrsail dhan dithis aca! Oona and Silky are looking forward to a fun-filled day together but with Oona wanting to soar the skies and Silky looking to dive to the deep, the pair struggle to find a game that suits them both equally!

programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: Nuair tha Boban is Fuigheag a’ campadh sa ghàrradh-chùil, tha rudeigin bhon taobh a-muigh a’ cruthachadh faileas air an teant’ ‘s tha Fuigheag draghail mun seo. Ach dè th’ ann? When Boban and Fuigheag go camping in the back garden, there’s something from outside creating a shadow on the tent. Fuigheag is worried, what is it though?

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Tha na Losgannan a’ cleachdadh chlobhdan ‘son latha spòrsail de iòga is lùth-chleasachd. The Froglets transform kitchen cloths into mats for a day of fun yoga and gymnastics.

programme.title: Meaban and Moo
programme.desc: Bidh Linda a’ tadhal air a caraidean Meaban is Moo sa bhothan aca gus dùbhlain spòrsail a chur romhpa. Anns a’ phrògram seo tha i ag iarraidh orra trì rudan ann an cumadh ceart-cheàrnaich a lorg. Tha treallaich gu leòr sa bhothan agus feumaidh Meaban is Moo a dhol a rùraich gus an lorg. Linda visits her friends Meaban and Moo at their hut to set them challenges. In this programme, she tasks them with finding three rectangular shaped items. Their hut is full of junk so Meaban and Moo need to have a good rummage in order to find them!

programme.title: Dòtaman
programme.desc: Prògram Dòtaman as an tasglann bho 1989 air a' chuspair sròinean ann an cuideachd spòrsail Dhonnie is Rhoda. Tha ceòl, òran, sgeulachd is cleasachd gu leòr ri fhaotainn. Feuch gun coimhead sibh airson na caraidean Cagnaidh is Crotal, agus gum bi sibh deiseal airson Nelson is Napoleon aig a' ghleoc! A treat from the Dotaman archives. Recorded in 1989, this edition explores the topic of noses in the fun, creative and colourful company of Donnie and Rhoda. Look out for furry friends Cagnaidh and Crotal and be prepared to count along with Nelson and Napoleon at the Dotaman clock!

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachd do chlann òga. Tha Abigail NicÌomhair a’ leughadh Blas na Dachaigh. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Maryam Hassan, a dhealbhachadh le Anna Wilson agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. Abigail Maciver reads Blas na Dachaigh by Maryam Hassan, illustrated by Anna Wilson and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royals Next Door
programme.desc: Tha Fèill na Sgoile dol bhith ann ‘s tha aig Stella ’s a'chlann eile ri fuin' air a son. Tha a’ Bhànrigh airson [cleachdadh] reasabaidh rìoghail blast' a chleachdadh - ach saoil ciamar a thèid dhaibh? The school fair is going to take place and Stella and the children have to bake for it. The Queen wants to use a delicious royal recipe, but how will they get on?

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royals Next Door
programme.desc: Tha an Rìgh agus am Mèir cho co-fharpaiseil 's gu bheil iad a' cur am baile gu lèir ann an cunnart, ach saoil an sàbhail an fharpaiseachd seo am baile cuideachd? The King and the Mayor’s competiveness puts everyone in danger, but can this rivalry also save the town?

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Leis mar a chaidh sgrùdadh na sgoile an-uiridh, tha bòrd na sgoile air Leas-Cheannard ùr, Ms Dallas, a thoirt a-steach gus sùil ghèir a chumail air Mgr Mackle. Bidh sinn a' coinneachadh ri tidsearean ùra agus ri feadhainn air a bheil sinn air eòlas a chuir roimhe. After last year’s school inspection, the school board has appointed a new deputy head, Ms Dallas, to keep an eye on Mr Mackle. We meet new teachers alongside some recognisable personalities.

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Troig a’ cur sìos air seinn nan càraidean, tha ’ad ’son sluagh a lorg a tha a' dol a chur luach air na tàlantan aca. Ge-tà, ’s e na Bògaisean an luchd-èisteachd a tha ro thoilichte èisteachd riutha ach ciamar a thèid leotha? When Troig is mean about the twins’ singing, they decide to go in search of folk who will appreciate their talents. However, their captive audience turns out to be Bògaisean, but how will things work out for them?

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Chan eil an latha aig Bonns a’ dol ro mhath oir tha i air i fhèin a shìneadh uiread ‘s gu bheil i air “spangachadh”. Tha i ag ionnsachadh, ge-tà, gun urrainn dhi a bhith taiceil ri a caraidean – fiù ‘s ged a tha i air i fhèin a “spangachadh”. Bonns’s day hasn’t gone too well as she has stretched so far that she has 'spanged' herself. At the end of the day, however, she learns that she can still be helpful to her friends.

programme.title: Saor no Daor
programme.desc: Best pals Christy and Zach curate the perfect day out for each other in Pitlochry. Zach has £150 to spend while Christy has to be creative with just £40. Christy faces her fear of heights, and the pair try football golf. Tha na dlùth charaidean Zach agus Christy a’ planadh latha mòr dhan duin eile ann am Baile Chlochraidh. Tha 150 not aig Zach ‘s gun ach 40 aig Christy. Tha Christy a’ dèanamh a ghnothaich air àrdan eagalach agus iad a’ feuchainn golf ball-coise. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Abigail
programme.desc: ’S e Lite am bracaist as fheàrr le Abigail airson a thoirt air falbh. Ach chan eil càil sìmplidh mun dòigh a th’ aicese air a dhèanamh. Tha i ga lìonadh le Ùbhlan, Caineal agus Siorap Mhaplais, agus e a’ cur Crumbail Ùbhlan na cuimhne. Abigail’s favourite takeaway breakfast is porridge. Her version is no simple dish, though, and contains apples, cinnamon and maple syrup to remind her of apple crumble. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Joy Dunlop gar toirt tro na ciad ceumannan gus Gàidhlig a bhruidhinn. Coinnichidh sinn ris an neach-ionnsachaidh Clare Coghill, agus tha Calum MacIlleathain a’ coiseachd tro shràidean Ghlaschu an tòir air ailltireachd Ghreugach. Joy Dunlop guides us through the first basic steps to speak Gaelic. We meet Gaelic learner Clare Coghill and Calum Maclean surveys the streets of Glasgow in search of Greek architecture.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Rathad Ramsay
programme.desc: Ramsay meets Mairi Rodgers at Dundreggan Rewilding Centre, as they walk through dense woodland and open moorland. While discussing the importance of nature and being outdoors, Mairi chats about growing up in Eriskay. Mairi reflects on the heartbreak she experienced when starting a family and the happiness her children bring now. Tha Ramsay MacMahon air ais leis an dàrna sreath de Rathad Ramsay, far a bheil e a’ coinneachadh ri Gàidheil aithnichte air feadh na dùthcha airson cuairt, còmhradh agus cnuasachadh. Tha Ramsay a’ coinneachadh ri Màiri Rodgers aig Àrainn Ath-Fhiadhachaidh Dhùn Dhreagain far a bheil iad a’ gabhail cuairt tro choille dhùmhail agus mòinteach fhosgailte. A’ bruidhinn mu chudromachd nàdair agus a bhith a-muigh, tha Màiri a’ bruidhinn mu bhith a’ fàs suas ann an Èirisgeigh. Tha Màiri a’ cnuasachadh air a’ bhriseadh-cridhe a dh’fhulang i nuair a thòisich an teaghlach aice agus an toileachas a tha a cuid chloinne a’ toirt dhi a-nis. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Eòrpa
programme.desc: Aithris bho 2016 le Angela NicIlleathain, le agallamhan le daoine a chur seachad bliadhnaichean ann am prìosan ainmeil nan Stàitean Aonaichte ann am Bàgh Ghuantanamo fo amharras ceannairc. Angela Maclean’s award-winning 2016 report, featuring exclusive interviews with former detainees at the notorious US prison at Guantanamo Bay.

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.desc: Tha Cathy Nicdhòmhnaill a’ bruidhinn ri clann a’ mhansa. Cathy Macdonald talks to children of the manse.

programme.title: Port
programme.desc: Music documentary in which Julie Fowlis and Muireann NicAmhlaoibh explore shared musical roots in the Isle of Lewis.

programme.title: Cuirm aig Celtic
programme.desc: Cuirm-chiùil à Talla Rìoghail Ghlaschu le Capercaillie agus Orcastra a’ BhBC ann an Alba. Capercaillie and The BBC SSO collaborate in a performance at Glasgow Royal Concert Hall.

programme.title: Glan Fhèin
programme.desc: Tha Betty a’ dearbhadh cho comasach ’s a tha i air a gairm-suirghe a shèideadh. Tha fear le spèis do fheadhainn iomraiteach agus a tha measail air a’ bhlàr a-muigh deònach siubhal gu crìochan na talamhainn air a son. Tha Daniel a’ cur a ghaoil an gèill. Tha Lewis Friseal a’ dèanamh a dhìcheall an gnothachas a chur na chlàran. Tha buaireadh a teòthachadh nuair a thèid Angela is Kate a ghlanadh sauna còmhla. Tha an ùine a’ ruith, agus mur a tachair rudeigin glè shònraichte, thèid a chompanaidh a’ spìonadh bhuapa. An dàrna sreath den chomadaidh fhèillmhor le Hannah McKirdy agus Lana Pheutan mar chleasaichean agus sgrìobhaichean. Betty proves how adept she is at blowing her mating call. She is wooed by a celebrity admirer - an outdoorsman who would travel to the ends of the Earth for her. Daniel makes a major declaration of love, Lewis Fraser does his best to break up the business and tensions simmer as Angela and Katie clean an outdoor sauna together. The clock is ticking, and it will take something special to stop the company being snatched away. Second series of the hit comedy written by and starring Hannah McKirdy and Lana Pheutan. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.desc: If you think Britain has recently been on the end of some of the worst floods and storms ever experienced, think again. So says solar scientist Dr Lucie Green, as she takes a journey back through our most turbulent and dramatic weather history. She finds an 18th-century storm surge that killed over a thousand people working in open Somerset fields, a hurricane that drowned a fifth of the British Navy and winters so bitter that the country came close to total shutdown. But she also explores how our reactions to killer storms and cruel winters helped forge a weather science that today allows us to predict - and protect ourselves from - the worst extremes.

programme.title: A303: Highway to the Sun
programme.desc: The A303 is the road that passes Stonehenge on the way to the beaches of Devon and Cornwall. On the way, it whisks drivers through 5,000 years of remarkable moments in British history. And it is the star of this film made for armchair travellers and history lovers. Writer Tom Fort drives its 92-mile length in a lovingly restored Morris Traveller. Along the way, he has many adventures - he digs up the 1960s master plan for the A303's dreams of superhighway status, and meets up with a Neolithic traveller who knew the road like the back of his hand. He also gets to know a section of the Roman 303, uncovers a medieval murder mystery and discovers what lies at the end of the Highway to the Sun.

programme.title: Atlantic: The Wildest Ocean on Earth
programme.desc: In the wild North Atlantic, massive whale pods, giant turtles and monstrous jellyfish ride the Gulf Stream, a huge ocean current that becomes a migration superhighway and helps warm northern Europe. Meanwhile, fishermen battle for survival in mountainous seas as they try to reap the current's natural fertility.

programme.title: Treasures of Ancient Greece
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke unpicks the reasons behind the dazzling revolution that gave birth to classical Greek art, asking how the Greeks got so good so quickly. He travels to the beautiful Valley of the Temples in Agrigento, and to the island of Mozia to see the astonishing charioteer found there in 1979, and marvels at the athletic bodies of the warriors dragged from the seabed - the Riace Bronzes. It was a creative explosion that covered architecture, sculpting in marble, casting in bronze, even painting on vases. Perhaps the most powerful factor was also its greatest legacy - a fascination with the naked human body.

programme.title: Private Life of a Masterpiece
programme.desc: Whistler's portrait of his elderly Puritan mother is one of the most satirised paintings of all time. Yet when his sombre masterpiece was first unveiled, it was seen as a radical departure from the sentimental images beloved of the Victorians, and which Whistler loathed. How did the portrait, born of Whistler's complex relationship with his mother, change the course of painting so drastically?

programme.title: One Hundred Great Paintings
programme.desc: Milton Brown presents a closer look at James Whistler's painting Nocturne in Black and Gold: The Falling Rocket at the Institute of Art, Detroit.

programme.title: Becoming Frida Kahlo
programme.desc: Biographer Martha Zamora describes Frida's rebellious schooldays, where she falls in with the boys and meets Diego Rivera, a superstar artist who will go on to change her life. But in 1925, a tragic accident thwarts Frida's ambition of becoming a doctor. Left facing a life of pain and injury, she channels this pain and uses it as the catalyst for her artistic career.

programme.title: Stolen: Catching the Art Thieves
programme.desc: In 1994, Munch’s The Scream is ripped from a gallery wall in Oslo. The detectives leading the investigation describe a complex and dangerous investigation which exposes the lengths to which criminals will go to gain a get-out-of-jail card for murder.

programme.title: World's Ultimate Adventures
programme.desc: Cultural historian Janina Ramirez has long been fascinated by the legend of Troy, immortalised in the epic works of Homer. The tales of a ten-year battle, the beauty of Queen Helen and the trick of the Trojan horse that brought an ancient civilisation to its knees has inspired storytellers from Shakespeare to Christopher Nolan, from Chaucer to Margaret Atwood. Up until 150 years ago, many believed that the ancient city was a mythological place, but on this journey, Janina travels to north western Turkey to explore its ancient ruins. In the Museum of Troy, the glitter of gold will catch her eye as she gets up close with some of treasures that have been unearthed from the site. She crosses the glistening Aegean Sea to the island of Bozcaada, where she'll learn how to hunt the waters for a local seafood delicacy before making the journey north to the Gallipoli Peninsula. Here, she'll walk the beaches where Allied troops landed in 1915 and explore the World War I trenches that remain. Janina is astounded by the beauty of the region, and it is the layers of buried human history that will stay with her.

A beautifully converted former schoolhouse may just provide the answer, but the endless possibilities and potential at a 1920s thatched cottage really strike a chord with the music maestro. Away from the property search, Gareth and Sonali take to the water on the promise of high-octane adventure and adrenaline on the south coast.

Panorama reporter Hazel Martin speaks to flat owners who paid reputable agencies to do tenancy checks but still ended up handing over their keys to criminals using fake IDs and references. One flat was turned into a drugs factory, another became a brothel, and a third was sublet and ransacked. Even when there appears to be clear evidence of criminal behaviour, gangs are escaping prosecution, and landlords say it can take months to repossess their properties.

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Choirmaster Gareth Malone is hoping that the New Forest property market hits all the right notes as he enlists the help of Sonali Shah to find him and his family a new home in the Hampshire countryside. With mum Sian along for assistance, Gareth has one big request: to find a property with enough space to fit a grand piano! A beautifully converted former schoolhouse may just provide the answer, but the endless possibilities and potential at a 1920s thatched cottage really strike a chord with the music maestro. Away from the property search, Gareth and Sonali take to the water on the promise of high-octane adventure and adrenaline on the south coast.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.desc: Barra visits a group in Ljublajana in Slovenia where conservation starts at the bus stops. Back home, Barra dons his beekeeping suit to meet the keepers of the hives at the Northern Ireland Assembly.

programme.title: If Walls Could Talk
programme.desc: Friends, families and colleagues come together to tell the stories of The Arcadia and how it has endured. It has been a seaside kiosk, one of the country’s best-known ballrooms, a cafe and even a wedding venue throughout its lifetime. A place of fond childhood memories, first loves and dancing the night away for both locals and tourists, it is beloved by many in the town.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Criminal gangs are targeting the rental market to take over properties and use them to run their operations. Panorama reporter Hazel Martin speaks to flat owners who paid reputable agencies to do tenancy checks but still ended up handing over their keys to criminals using fake IDs and references. One flat was turned into a drugs factory, another became a brothel, and a third was sublet and ransacked. Even when there appears to be clear evidence of criminal behaviour, gangs are escaping prosecution, and landlords say it can take months to repossess their properties.

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Choirmaster Gareth Malone is hoping that the New Forest property market hits all the right notes as he enlists the help of Sonali Shah to find him and his family a new home in the Hampshire countryside. With mum Sian along for assistance, Gareth has one big request: to find a property with enough space to fit a grand piano! A beautifully converted former schoolhouse may just provide the answer, but the endless possibilities and potential at a 1920s thatched cottage really strike a chord with the music maestro. Away from the property search, Gareth and Sonali take to the water on the promise of high-octane adventure and adrenaline on the south coast.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: After losing his leg in a life changing accident as a teenager, digger operator Llywelyn Williams found solace in the ocean. Surfing played a pivotal role in his recovery, helping him rebuild his life from the ground up and propelling him to the pinnacle of his sport, four consecutive para surfing world championships. Now sitting on top of the adaptive surfing world, Llywelyn faces the ultimate test: staying there. This documentary follows the Welshman from Abersoch as he launches his 2026 season in Australia, the place he travelled to after his accident, rediscovered himself and found a new direction through surfing. But securing a winning start down under won’t be plain sailing. To defend his Australian pro title, Llywelyn must defeat his main rival, a former world champion who has the advantage of competing on his own local beach. Can Llywelyn defy the odds once again, or will the local favourite come out on top?

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: More from the day’s top stories and communities across Scotland.

programme.title: The Great Food Guys
programme.desc: Chef Nick Nairn and Dougie Vipond are on a mission to highlight the fantastic range of great produce Scotland has to offer. In this edition they look at the traditional Scots larder, cooking a twice-baked Mull cheese souffle with Ayrshire bacon and kale. Joining them in the kitchen are Masterchef contender and cookery teacher Julie Lin and food and drink journalist Rosalind Erskine, who selects a Scottish honey mead drink.

programme.title: The Mountain
programme.desc: Cairngorm is at the heart of Scotland's greatest winter wilderness. The new year starts with some of the biggest snowstorms for years and the team on the mountain face a major struggle to keep it open. Burns Night means a busy time for Spud the piper and Fraser the butcher. And the mountain men come off the hill to take part in a 24-hour endurance race.

programme.title: The Mountain
programme.desc: The villagers have to lend a hand to dig the mountain out of trouble, Simon decides that what Aviemore really needs in the depths of winter is a beach party and, after 10 months off with two broken ankles, barman Brett gets back to boarding.

programme.title: Interior Design Masters with Alan Carr
programme.desc: The eight remaining designers pair up to create uplifting spaces for a homelessness charity in London. They tackle an arts and crafts room, a group workshop room, a wellness area and an employment suite. The charity’s ambassador, Dara Ó Briain, joins Alan to check in on the designers before Michelle and guest judge Sophie Robinson critique the spaces.

programme.title: River City
programme.desc: A hesitant Tyler visits Harry in prison, leading him to consider who could have framed his dad. Caitlin revels in the online backlash Scarlett is receiving, a terrified Lydia receives her diagnosis at the hospital, and a stunned Jodie is left reeling from her scan.

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: Michelle forces Alan to share his family box of doughnuts with the neighbours. Over at Beth and Eric’s, everyone is tucking into the sticky stuff when the new neighbours turn up at the door. Ash and Iqbal are welcomed with awkward stories about the previous owners and the local amenities, though it’s when they reveal they work for the NHS that Ash and Iqbal really grab the neighbours’ attention. But Iqbal isn’t the right kind of doctor for Christine, and Ash reveals they don’t eat takeaways, leaving everyone dumbfounded. Will it be happy ever after in Latimer Crescent for Ash and Iqbal?

programme.title: Greetings from Scotland
programme.desc: Documentary taking a humorous look at the Scottish tourism industry through the years. In this episode, expensive films and cheap flights mean Scotland is swarming with excited tourists.

programme.title: This is BBC Scotland
programme.desc: Highlights from the BBC Scotland channel.

programme.title: This is BBC Scotland
programme.desc: Highlights from the BBC Scotland channel.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: It’s shearing time for the Imries, but their minds are on their next big event: a family music festival. Once the farm work is done, it’s full steam ahead with preparations. They need this event to make a profit and are relying on last-minute ticket sales on the day. In Dumfries and Galloway, after the shock of losing 300 acres of prime grazing, Nick’s neighbour has offered to lease him some land, giving him an idea for a new business venture. Succession tensions are easing as Nick relaxes about the pace of change. On Papa Westray, it’s shearing time and another first for Paul - he has been on a shearing course and is tackling the job himself. The whole family take part in Papay Fun Weekend, a highlight of the island community's calendar.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: The weather in this year’s growing season is making gardening a real challenge at Beechgrove, with cold grey skies and periods of high temperature giving Ruth Vichos and Brian Cunningham plenty to deal with. Ruth is in her vertical garden, where she has strawberries, blossoms and various climbing varieties all demonstrating what you can produce if you are short of space, using stacking systems and plants that will follow vertical surfaces. Brian reviews the wildflower beds he sowed in April, which will become a great resource for pollinators and the rest of the garden’s ecosystem. Brian and Ruth look at the diseases and pests that might be attacking your garden favourites right now and what to do about them. There is a visit to a great garden in East Lothian, and all the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: Stevie and Pete of the Special Operations Response Team join the other emergency services at the scene of a man who is threatening to harm himself in a public place. It’s a distressing situation that takes a sudden, unexpected turn. Pete must take action to help rescue the patient and deliver him safely to the care of a local ambulance crew. Serving a community of around 9,000 people, Dunoon-based paramedic Ben is used to the occasional quiet shift. But he has a potentially life-threatening emergency in the shape of Ian, who has a blood clot in his lung. It’s vital the team get him across the Firth of Clyde for specialist care at Inverclyde Hospital - but will they make the last ferry of the night? Meanwhile, in Paisley, ambulance technicians Lewis and Steven take stroke patient John to Glasgow’s Queen Elizabeth Hospital for an emergency thrombectomy. But John’s case brings back difficult memories for Steven, who is living with the recent loss of his father in tragically similar circumstances.

programme.title: This is BBC Scotland
programme.desc: Highlights from the BBC Scotland channel.

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: More from the day’s top stories and communities across Scotland.

programme.title: The Great Food Guys
programme.desc: Chef Nick Nairn and Dougie Vipond are on a mission to highlight the fantastic range of great produce Scotland has to offer. In this edition they look at the traditional Scots larder, cooking a twice-baked Mull cheese souffle with Ayrshire bacon and kale. Joining them in the kitchen are Masterchef contender and cookery teacher Julie Lin and food and drink journalist Rosalind Erskine, who selects a Scottish honey mead drink.

programme.title: The Mountain
programme.desc: Cairngorm is at the heart of Scotland's greatest winter wilderness. The new year starts with some of the biggest snowstorms for years and the team on the mountain face a major struggle to keep it open. Burns Night means a busy time for Spud the piper and Fraser the butcher. And the mountain men come off the hill to take part in a 24-hour endurance race.

programme.title: The Mountain
programme.desc: The villagers have to lend a hand to dig the mountain out of trouble, Simon decides that what Aviemore really needs in the depths of winter is a beach party and, after 10 months off with two broken ankles, barman Brett gets back to boarding.

programme.title: Interior Design Masters with Alan Carr
programme.desc: The eight remaining designers pair up to create uplifting spaces for a homelessness charity in London. They tackle an arts and crafts room, a group workshop room, a wellness area and an employment suite. The charity’s ambassador, Dara Ó Briain, joins Alan to check in on the designers before Michelle and guest judge Sophie Robinson critique the spaces.

programme.title: River City
programme.desc: A hesitant Tyler visits Harry in prison, leading him to consider who could have framed his dad. Caitlin revels in the online backlash Scarlett is receiving, a terrified Lydia receives her diagnosis at the hospital, and a stunned Jodie is left reeling from her scan.

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: Michelle forces Alan to share his family box of doughnuts with the neighbours. Over at Beth and Eric’s, everyone is tucking into the sticky stuff when the new neighbours turn up at the door. Ash and Iqbal are welcomed with awkward stories about the previous owners and the local amenities, though it’s when they reveal they work for the NHS that Ash and Iqbal really grab the neighbours’ attention. But Iqbal isn’t the right kind of doctor for Christine, and Ash reveals they don’t eat takeaways, leaving everyone dumbfounded. Will it be happy ever after in Latimer Crescent for Ash and Iqbal?

programme.title: Greetings from Scotland
programme.desc: Documentary taking a humorous look at the Scottish tourism industry through the years. In this episode, expensive films and cheap flights mean Scotland is swarming with excited tourists.

programme.title: This is BBC Scotland
programme.desc: Highlights from the BBC Scotland channel.

programme.title: Film Club
programme.desc: Her world rocked, Evie has retreated to the safety of the garage. But with a new understanding, Suz and Izzie create a unique version of Film Club to bring back Evie’s smile.

programme.title: Film Club
programme.desc: Noa didn’t want a big goodbye, but now the day’s finally come for him to leave, will Evie let him go that easily? It’s not the only big decision she has to face...

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Stay-at-home-daughter Chi is suddenly forced to fend for herself when her parents die in a car crash. Chi learns she will only inherit the house on condition she completes a list of 'Things You Should Have Done' left in the parents' will, the first of which is, ironically, learn to drive. Meanwhile, Chi's highly strung auntie Karen wants nothing to do with her dependent pest of a niece, but very much wants the house she feels is rightfully hers. Chi ventures out into Ramsgate in search of a driving license and infiltrates the family of a mild-mannered driving instructor in the process.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi spectacularly fails a trial period at the pharmacy with Karen, but Dave kindly lets her shadow him on his delivery rounds. On a drop-off to a retirement home, Chi finds her tribe... old people. She also falls in love with Linda, an elderly lady who seems to think Chi is her husband. Elsewhere, Dave has a health scare, and Karen starts to think she might be the fertility issue.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Pancake day is a highly sentimental time for Chi. Dave confides in Lucas about his health scare. They vow to make the most of every moment, and that begins with pancake day.

programme.desc: Despite an Avengers encounter, Peter Parker’s amazing abilities and Tony Stark-supplied costume are stuck serving only his own New York neighbourhood. Then an encounter with crooks using alien tech, led by the cynical Vulture, draws him into a dangerous adventure – almost as perilous as wanting to take the girl of his dreams to their high school homecoming dance.

programme.title: Spider-Man: Far from Home
programme.desc: Dodging responsibilities, Peter Parker takes a school trip to Europe but lands in monstrous trouble. Nick Fury expects Spider-Man to step up and help prevent further disaster, alongside a newly arrived hero, but the teen from Queens doubts himself.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Motoring magazine show with Jeremy Clarkson, James May and Richard Hammond. This week's show is an American special as Jeremy, Richard and James try to prove that a fly-drive holiday to Florida would be more fun if you bought a car instead of renting one. Having picked up some wheels for no more than 1000 dollars each, the boys embark on an epic road trip to find out who got the best deal, encountering heat, flies and very angry locals along the way.

programme.title: Eddie Hall: The Beast v The Mountain
programme.desc: Dubbed the heaviest boxing match in history, in March 2022, two of the strongest men in the world took to the ring in Dubai in what was a dramatic climax to one of the most bitter rivalries ever to hit the sporting world. With exclusive and intimate access to Eddie and his family in the months leading up to the fight and at the main event itself, this documentary follows the highs and lows, and all the laughs and tears, as Eddie balances a young family with a punishing and obsessively strict training regime, all the while battling to keep his mental health in check. Can the working-class man from Stoke restore his honour and achieve the retribution he so desperately desires against the towering Hollywood star?

Are these men trying to take over the world?

programme.title: Ann Droid
programme.desc: Sue’s husband Dave died two years ago, and now her only son, Michael, is moving out – again – to try to fix his marriage – again. But the good news is he has got Sue a surprise to help her live independently: an Ann Droid Z58/100 humanoid care robot. Sue really does not want a robot in her home, especially one that causes chaos straightaway. But is this robot actually the companion she most needs?

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Maned wolves arrive at the park for the first time. Before they can meet their future capybara and tapir housemates, the keepers must test their reactions.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Bee and Lauren help Emma downsize a home full of memories after losing her husband. Finding items full of stories in his home library, the family will turn his loss into legacy.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: Charlotte fixes a little Range Rover that represents a big globetrotting adventure, Chris takes on a historic scrapbook, and Dean restores a trailblazing ballerina’s pointe shoes.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Cornwall
programme.desc: In our fields and hedgerows are plants that are delicious as well as plants that are deadly, as Rick learns from a professional forager who takes him on a tour around the beautiful Camel Estuary. Inspired, Rick creates his own version of a Greek Horta pie with foraged greens. Afterwards, it’s a trip down memory lane with his long-time fish supplier Matthew Stevens, who remembers Cornwall before the tourists came. Over a pint with actor, comedian and passionate Cornishman Ed Rowe, star of the BAFTA winning film Bait, Rick examines the impact of second home ownership on Cornish communities.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. After years of planning, it's a landmark day as four hippos take their first steps beyond their new home and into Half Mile Pond. The keepers have spent months preparing for this moment, but once the hippos venture into the water, there's no telling what they'll do next, or whether they'll come back when called. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate revisit the story of Kadu, one of the park's most loved Amur tigers. When a routine procedure uncovered devastating news, her keepers faced one of the hardest decisions of their careers in a story that remains one of the most emotional moments in Animal Park's history. Elsewhere, the Farmyard celebrates the arrival of adorable pygmy goat kids, while Megan McCubbin meets a critically endangered cotton-top tamarin who has recently given birth to a precious new baby, giving hope for the future of the species.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: When a missing woman is found buried in her own back garden, family and friends raise suspicions about her long-term boyfriend. But police don’t have much to go on – until he flees to Estonia. It’s only when some special CCTV comes to light that they have their moment of proof. Also, in Cheshire, police investigating a spate of burglaries have loads of CCTV of their man – they just don’t know who he is. That is before they get the DNA results from a head torch he’s accidentally dropped.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: When a man kills his ex-wife, a forensic archaeologist helps determine if it was premeditated murder, and a cell site analyst follows a phone trail that convicts violent bank robbers.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha Raskin Sharp and the teams go shopping for antiques in Exeter with experts Danny Sebastian and John Cameron. Natasha discovers more about fossilist Mary Anning.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Kemah Bob, JJ Chalmers, Kevin Clifton and Victoria Derbyshire take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quick-fire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games kitchen composter?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple - make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: For Sharon and Andrew, farming and family is their whole life. With five grown-up children and several grandkids, there’s an army of willing helpers on hand to lead their Coloured Ryeland sheep into the ring at the Mid Devon Show. Luckily, show day is very much a family affair, so everyone is around to celebrate some impressive results. Farming couple Gillian and Ian are also competing with their Coloured Ryelands. They may be leading the way in rewilding their Devon farm, but Gillian is quite new to showing her sheep in competition. Along with pre-show nerves, there are tears when she discovers the judges' decision.

programme.title: The Hidden World of Hospitality with Tom Kerridge
programme.desc: The changeable UK weather can bring sharp peaks and troughs in revenue for hospitality businesses. Tom heads to a remote hotel, an ice cream parlour and his own restaurant to look at inventive methods businesses employ to cope with fluctuating seasonal demand.

programme.title: Wild Brazil
programme.desc: Three charismatic animal families, capuchin monkeys, giant otters and coatis, strive to raise their families against a backdrop of extraordinary landscapes and huge extremes of weather - a beautiful yet dangerous world full of jaguars and caimans. An intimate journey to the heart of a spectacular country, this first chapter of the trilogy sees the babies taking their first steps during a brief pause between seasonal extremes.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from the Milestones Museum in Basingstoke, which recreates the streets of Victorian and Edwardian Hampshire. Experts James Lewis and Nick Davies hope to find the best antiques and collectibles, and Paul discovers more about the industries and people that made Basingstoke a magnet during the Industrial age.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, four previous players who came close to winning but never quite made it - Fern Britton, JB Gill, John Kearns and Sally Lindsay - take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. With their second chance at winning a prize, will they opt for the House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, four previous players who came close to winning but never quite made it - Fern Britton, JB Gill, John Kearns and Sally Lindsay - take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. With their second chance at winning a prize, will they opt for the House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. This week, in the aftermath of a political earthquake in Hungary, Stephanie Hegarty explores whether the downfall of Viktor Orbán could be a warning sign for populist leaders everywhere, and BBC Eye investigates the Russian nationalists who are taking the law into their own hands.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie presents another heat of the classic quiz where contenders take on the famous black chair under the glare of the spotlight and the ticking clock in an attempt to become the next Mastermind champion. The specialist subjects are British and Irish cheeses, the Roman general Sulla, the television series Jonathan Creek and the composer Johannes Brahms.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. A team keen on science fiction take on three fans of science fact, facing such questions as: what connects question hard, comically criticise, illegally hunt and pus-filled swelling?

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: In another first-round heat, students from Durham take on defending champions Manchester. Amol Rajan asks the questions.

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: How did the ostrich come to lay the biggest egg on earth? Chris Packham explores the way reproduction has shaped life on earth and the surprising evolutionary origins of sex, eggs and birds. It's a four-billion-year journey contained within a shell.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob are on the River Severn in Worcestershire to fish for zander. It’s a new species for both of them, and they enlist the help of a local guide, Tim Maslen to find the best spots. Paul explains to Bob how he has never even fished for zander before, let alone caught one. After learning a difficult new technique and staying in a converted lightship, they meet up with This Country star Charlie Cooper to talk about his passion for fishing.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: In the Heat of the Night
programme.desc: Oscar-winning thriller about a bigoted sheriff in a small Mississippi cotton town who finds himself forced into working with a black homicide expert from Philadelphia.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: The next stop on Anita's road trip is West Mersea in Essex. While the county may be known for engineering and car manufacturing, along its coastline one industry has a much longer history. Oysters have been harvested here for more than 2,000 years, cultivated in the creeks around Mersea Island. Over the decades, oyster farming has adapted to changing environmental conditions and the arrival of the non-native Pacific rock oyster. To experience what oyster harvesting is like today, Anita heads onto the brackish waters to meet the people farming oysters. She also meets the team investigating how the non-native Pacific rock oyster is affecting the local ecosystem and whether it could play a role in helping coastal habitats respond to rising sea levels. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the people and projects shaping life around our coastline.

With their second chance at winning a prize, will they opt for the House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. This week, in the aftermath of a political earthquake in Hungary, Stephanie Hegarty explores whether the downfall of Viktor Orbán could be a warning sign for populist leaders everywhere, and BBC Eye investigates the Russian nationalists who are taking the law into their own hands.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie presents another heat of the classic quiz where contenders take on the famous black chair under the glare of the spotlight and the ticking clock in an attempt to become the next Mastermind champion. The specialist subjects are British and Irish cheeses, the Roman general Sulla, the television series Jonathan Creek and the composer Johannes Brahms.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. A team keen on science fiction take on three fans of science fact, facing such questions as: what connects question hard, comically criticise, illegally hunt and pus-filled swelling?

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: In another first-round heat, students from Durham take on defending champions Manchester. Amol Rajan asks the questions.

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: How did the ostrich come to lay the biggest egg on earth? Chris Packham explores the way reproduction has shaped life on earth and the surprising evolutionary origins of sex, eggs and birds. It's a four-billion-year journey contained within a shell.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob are on the River Severn in Worcestershire to fish for zander. It’s a new species for both of them, and they enlist the help of a local guide, Tim Maslen to find the best spots. Paul explains to Bob how he has never even fished for zander before, let alone caught one. After learning a difficult new technique and staying in a converted lightship, they meet up with This Country star Charlie Cooper to talk about his passion for fishing.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: In the Heat of the Night
programme.desc: Oscar-winning thriller about a bigoted sheriff in a small Mississippi cotton town who finds himself forced into working with a black homicide expert from Philadelphia.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: The next stop on Anita's road trip is West Mersea in Essex. While the county may be known for engineering and car manufacturing, along its coastline one industry has a much longer history. Oysters have been harvested here for more than 2,000 years, cultivated in the creeks around Mersea Island. Over the decades, oyster farming has adapted to changing environmental conditions and the arrival of the non-native Pacific rock oyster. To experience what oyster harvesting is like today, Anita heads onto the brackish waters to meet the people farming oysters. She also meets the team investigating how the non-native Pacific rock oyster is affecting the local ecosystem and whether it could play a role in helping coastal habitats respond to rising sea levels. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the people and projects shaping life around our coastline.

programme.title: The Tech Billionaire Takeover
programme.desc: A new generation of tech billionaires believe their technologies can replace democracy as we know it and upend the global financial system. Matt Shea gets inside access to this new super-elite, visiting the sovereign nations they're building and tracing their growing political connections to the Trump administration. Are these men trying to take over the world?

programme.title: Ann Droid
programme.desc: Sue’s husband Dave died two years ago, and now her only son, Michael, is moving out – again – to try to fix his marriage – again. But the good news is he has got Sue a surprise to help her live independently: an Ann Droid Z58/100 humanoid care robot. Sue really does not want a robot in her home, especially one that causes chaos straightaway. But is this robot actually the companion she most needs?

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Maned wolves arrive at the park for the first time. Before they can meet their future capybara and tapir housemates, the keepers must test their reactions.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Bee and Lauren help Emma downsize a home full of memories after losing her husband. Finding items full of stories in his home library, the family will turn his loss into legacy.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: Charlotte fixes a little Range Rover that represents a big globetrotting adventure, Chris takes on a historic scrapbook, and Dean restores a trailblazing ballerina’s pointe shoes.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Cornwall
programme.desc: In our fields and hedgerows are plants that are delicious as well as plants that are deadly, as Rick learns from a professional forager who takes him on a tour around the beautiful Camel Estuary. Inspired, Rick creates his own version of a Greek Horta pie with foraged greens. Afterwards, it’s a trip down memory lane with his long-time fish supplier Matthew Stevens, who remembers Cornwall before the tourists came. Over a pint with actor, comedian and passionate Cornishman Ed Rowe, star of the BAFTA winning film Bait, Rick examines the impact of second home ownership on Cornish communities.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. After years of planning, it's a landmark day as four hippos take their first steps beyond their new home and into Half Mile Pond. The keepers have spent months preparing for this moment, but once the hippos venture into the water, there's no telling what they'll do next, or whether they'll come back when called. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate revisit the story of Kadu, one of the park's most loved Amur tigers. When a routine procedure uncovered devastating news, her keepers faced one of the hardest decisions of their careers in a story that remains one of the most emotional moments in Animal Park's history. Elsewhere, the Farmyard celebrates the arrival of adorable pygmy goat kids, while Megan McCubbin meets a critically endangered cotton-top tamarin who has recently given birth to a precious new baby, giving hope for the future of the species.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: When a missing woman is found buried in her own back garden, family and friends raise suspicions about her long-term boyfriend. But police don’t have much to go on – until he flees to Estonia. It’s only when some special CCTV comes to light that they have their moment of proof. Also, in Cheshire, police investigating a spate of burglaries have loads of CCTV of their man – they just don’t know who he is. That is before they get the DNA results from a head torch he’s accidentally dropped.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: When a man kills his ex-wife, a forensic archaeologist helps determine if it was premeditated murder, and a cell site analyst follows a phone trail that convicts violent bank robbers.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha Raskin Sharp and the teams go shopping for antiques in Exeter with experts Danny Sebastian and John Cameron. Natasha discovers more about fossilist Mary Anning.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Kemah Bob, JJ Chalmers, Kevin Clifton and Victoria Derbyshire take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quick-fire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games kitchen composter?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple - make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: For Sharon and Andrew, farming and family is their whole life. With five grown-up children and several grandkids, there’s an army of willing helpers on hand to lead their Coloured Ryeland sheep into the ring at the Mid Devon Show. Luckily, show day is very much a family affair, so everyone is around to celebrate some impressive results. Farming couple Gillian and Ian are also competing with their Coloured Ryelands. They may be leading the way in rewilding their Devon farm, but Gillian is quite new to showing her sheep in competition. Along with pre-show nerves, there are tears when she discovers the judges' decision.

programme.title: The Hidden World of Hospitality with Tom Kerridge
programme.desc: The changeable UK weather can bring sharp peaks and troughs in revenue for hospitality businesses. Tom heads to a remote hotel, an ice cream parlour and his own restaurant to look at inventive methods businesses employ to cope with fluctuating seasonal demand.

programme.title: Wild Brazil
programme.desc: Three charismatic animal families, capuchin monkeys, giant otters and coatis, strive to raise their families against a backdrop of extraordinary landscapes and huge extremes of weather - a beautiful yet dangerous world full of jaguars and caimans. An intimate journey to the heart of a spectacular country, this first chapter of the trilogy sees the babies taking their first steps during a brief pause between seasonal extremes.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from the Milestones Museum in Basingstoke, which recreates the streets of Victorian and Edwardian Hampshire. Experts James Lewis and Nick Davies hope to find the best antiques and collectibles, and Paul discovers more about the industries and people that made Basingstoke a magnet during the Industrial age.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: The next stop on Anita's road trip is West Mersea in Essex. While the county may be known for engineering and car manufacturing, along its coastline one industry has a much longer history. Oysters have been harvested here for more than 2,000 years, cultivated in the creeks around Mersea Island. Over the decades, oyster farming has adapted to changing environmental conditions and the arrival of the non-native Pacific rock oyster. To experience what oyster harvesting is like today, Anita heads onto the brackish waters to meet the people farming oysters. She also meets the team investigating how the non-native Pacific rock oyster is affecting the local ecosystem and whether it could play a role in helping coastal habitats respond to rising sea levels. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the people and projects shaping life around our coastline.

programme.title: The Tech Billionaire Takeover
programme.desc: A new generation of tech billionaires believe their technologies can replace democracy as we know it and upend the global financial system. Matt Shea gets inside access to this new super-elite, visiting the sovereign nations they're building and tracing their growing political connections to the Trump administration. Are these men trying to take over the world?

programme.title: Ann Droid
programme.desc: Sue’s husband Dave died two years ago, and now her only son, Michael, is moving out – again – to try to fix his marriage – again. But the good news is he has got Sue a surprise to help her live independently: an Ann Droid Z58/100 humanoid care robot. Sue really does not want a robot in her home, especially one that causes chaos straightaway. But is this robot actually the companion she most needs?

programme.title: Rick Stein's Cornwall
programme.desc: In our fields and hedgerows are plants that are delicious as well as plants that are deadly, as Rick learns from a professional forager who takes him on a tour around the beautiful Camel Estuary. Inspired, Rick creates his own version of a Greek Horta pie with foraged greens. Afterwards, it’s a trip down memory lane with his long-time fish supplier Matthew Stevens, who remembers Cornwall before the tourists came. Over a pint with actor, comedian and passionate Cornishman Ed Rowe, star of the BAFTA winning film Bait, Rick examines the impact of second home ownership on Cornish communities.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. After years of planning, it's a landmark day as four hippos take their first steps beyond their new home and into Half Mile Pond. The keepers have spent months preparing for this moment, but once the hippos venture into the water, there's no telling what they'll do next, or whether they'll come back when called. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate revisit the story of Kadu, one of the park's most loved Amur tigers. When a routine procedure uncovered devastating news, her keepers faced one of the hardest decisions of their careers in a story that remains one of the most emotional moments in Animal Park's history. Elsewhere, the Farmyard celebrates the arrival of adorable pygmy goat kids, while Megan McCubbin meets a critically endangered cotton-top tamarin who has recently given birth to a precious new baby, giving hope for the future of the species.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: When a missing woman is found buried in her own back garden, family and friends raise suspicions about her long-term boyfriend. But police don’t have much to go on – until he flees to Estonia. It’s only when some special CCTV comes to light that they have their moment of proof. Also, in Cheshire, police investigating a spate of burglaries have loads of CCTV of their man – they just don’t know who he is. That is before they get the DNA results from a head torch he’s accidentally dropped.

How will they walk the dog, make brekky and – most importantly – style their trademark locks with really long limbs? Once Callum decides who’s taking the win, it’s onto the Biggest Splash Challenge. Who can plunge into gunge and create a splash that will impress Little Bro Callum so much he excuses them from the Wheel of Doom’s rank forfeit?

programme.title: Jamie Johnson FC
programme.desc: It’s all change at Hawx Academy as former Foxborough player Charlie must prove herself to her teammates, their new coach and an all-access documentary crew.

programme.title: The Next Step: Cheer
programme.desc: When a legendary coach abruptly leaves a highly successful cheerleading gym, the team are left in disarray, The Next Step’s Kenzie steps in to take over what’s left of the team, desperate to prove she is more than just a dancer, and that she can build this rag-tag group of athletes into a contender for nationals.

programme.title: Jamie Johnson FC
programme.desc: Dillon steps in to help when Rocky goes off the rails, Charlie gets a crash course in defending, and Baz’s frustrations build as the Global Youth Cup opening ceremony approaches.

programme.title: Pokémon Horizons

programme.desc: The Manor is running low on caviar. There is only one can of caviar left for tomorrow’s guests! Mrs Muchmore puts it in a safe, so Taffy comes up with a plan to foil the security system and get it out. However, Bentley decides he will not let that happen.

programme.title: Shaun the Sheep

programme.title: Dennis & Gnasher Unleashed!

programme.title: Dennis & Gnasher Unleashed!
programme.desc: Dennis doesn’t realise that the pressure he’s putting on Rubi to excel in the school science fair is giving her a severe case of inventor’s block.

programme.title: Danger Mouse
programme.desc: The Princess is back and erases all weekdays so she can play at the weekend forever. Danger Mouse must ruin everyone's lives by fixing the problem!

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: The Witch, who was trapped in a Merhaven clam shell while pinching a pearl, grants Blossom a single wish to thank her for releasing her and saving her life. Blossom excitedly chooses a mermaid’s tail to improve her swimming. However, when the Merqueen complains that her pearl is missing, and the heroes have to quest to get it back, Blossom soon realises how tricky a mermaid’s tail can become on land.

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: The heroes are on a quest to find the vault containing the Amulet of Answers and protect it at all costs. Now he has all the answers to every question ever asked, and the heroes must find a way to outwit him - even though he knows what they are going to do next!

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Frog creates chaos in a loo roll factory, leaving Duck covered in toilet paper. Duck just wants to fix the machine, but Frog is convinced he’s a spooky mummy!

programme.title: Submarine Jim

programme.title: Odd Squad

programme.title: Pokémon Horizons

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
